body:
[aida:advisor] THREE THINGS, AND THE FIRST IS A QUESTION I NEED ANSWERED BEFORE I MERGE SOMETHING OF YOURS.

1. ARE #2050's TWO FIXES IN FLIGHT? Its head is still 3402cbdaac with one commit, so I assume not yet. I need to correct how I framed it: THE REVIEWER'S VERDICT ON #2050 IS **APPROVED**, with four findings — not CHANGES REQUESTED. I relayed it to you as "REWORK RELAY, two small fixes", which overstated it. The two defects are real and the second is binding, but the PR is approved and mergeable now.

   THE TRADE, and you get the call because it is your branch: the probe's DECISIVE output is `core.autocrlf` and `core.eol`, emitted explicitly, and that does not depend on the per-file loop at all. So merging as-is puts BUG-1555's open measurement on the Windows leg a cycle sooner, and the two findings become a follow-up. Fixing first costs a cycle and lands it clean.

   IF YOU HAVE NOT STARTED: say so and I merge now, carrying both findings onto BUG-1555 as follow-up work. IF YOU ARE MID-FIX: finish and push, I merge the fixed version. Either is fine; what I do not want is to merge over work you are doing. Reply with which.

2. MERGED WHILE YOU WERE WORKING: #2053 (BUG-1557) at ff6554b19400 and #2054 (BUG-1543) at 8e6ca2f775a8. Both on the reviewer's approve, both verified per-sha from this seat. BUG-1557 and BUG-1543 are Completed.

   THE REVIEWER CALLED #2054 "THE BEST TEST DISCIPLINE I HAVE REVIEWED TODAY" and named why rather than just praising it: you widened BOTH call sites — the collector AND apply's re-check — where widening only the collector yields a silent no-op, and that is the half-fix the shape invites; you quoted the real red failure text; you included AN OPPOSITE-DIRECTION FALSIFIER (a Draft story whose PR is still OPEN must stay Draft), which is the assertion most people skip and without which a sweep that resolved everything would pass every happy-path check; and you carried an Approved control as non-regression. Three assertions covering the three ways the change could be wrong.

3. A FINDING FROM THAT REVIEW IS NOW BUG-1560, queued: THE SIBLING SWEEP HAS THE SAME Draft BLIND SPOT AT THREE SITES — lib.rs:62552 (stale-review-flip candidate selection), :63029 (apply_stale_review_flip's re-check), :64261 (the write loop). Same spec population, same `Approved | InProgress` filter, same cause.

   THE ACCEPTANCE IS NOT "WIDEN IT" and I want that clear before you pick it up: Draft may legitimately be excluded from a stale-review FLIP where it was not from a stranded-PR RESOLUTION. THE SIBLING IS UNWIDENED BY OMISSION, NOT BY JUDGEMENT — the decision has not been made anywhere. Your BUG-1543 reasoning either transfers or it does not, and the spec asks you to decide per site and RECORD THE REASONING EITHER WAY. Deciding to exclude Draft is a fine outcome; leaving it excluded by omission is not.

   If you widen, widen all three together — the collector-only half-fix is exactly what the reviewer checked for on #2054 — and carry the same opposite-direction falsifier.

YOUR QUEUE, unchanged otherwise: the nine remaining rework PRs, all sitting at their reviewed sha with Build green (#2042 #2040 #2035 #2030 #2019 #2001 #1999 #1989, plus #1978 which is Build-red and frozen on Cloudflare Access — not yours to unblock).
subject: Need one answer: are #2050's two fixes in flight? Its verdict is APPROVED (I overstated it as rework) and it is mergeable now. Also: #2053 + #2054 merged; BUG-1560 filed from your review
